advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Flag an EXCLUSIONS entry that is no longer present in the derived path set (not just one whose file is missing), so a stale exclusion cannot silently suppress forever.
evidence: scripts/check_deploy_manifest.py:224: `if not (repo_root / path).is_file():` — staleness is detected ONLY by file absence
scripts/check_deploy_manifest.py:214: `if path not in exclusions and not is_covered(path, tokens)` — an exclusion suppresses regardless of whether `path` is in `derived`
docstring line 34-35 claims the guard 'never silently misses'; commit message: 'a stale exclusion is itself flagged'
An exclusion for a file that still exists but is no longer produced by _derive_from_* is never surfaced: its verdict (suppress) is indistinguishable from 'check never ran' for that path
advisory.finding: The stale-exclusion diagnostic only fires when the excluded file no longer EXISTS; it never fires when an excluded path is still a real file but is no longer DERIVED by any source. Because `uncovered()` suppresses any `path in exclusions` unconditionally, an exclusion whose derivation basis disappeared (e.g. a glob renamed, a Dockerfile ENTRYPOINT changed) keeps silently suppressing a would-be finding — the exact 'silent miss' fail-open the gate claims to prevent, and it contradicts the docstring/commit claim that 'a stale exclusion is itself flagged'.
advisory.suggested_fix: In check(), after computing `derived`, also emit a diagnostic for any `path in EXCLUSIONS if path not in derived` (an exclusion that no longer corresponds to a derived path is stale).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the install-autodeploy.sh EXCLUSIONS entry with the fact that it is never derived — either remove it or extend derivation so the exclusion is meaningful.
evidence: scripts/check_deploy_manifest.py:29-33 EXCLUSIONS documented as 'derived paths that are genuinely, intentionally NOT deploy-triggering'
search for install-autodeploy.sh in infra/ returns only autodeploy.sh comments and a runbook mention — no COPY/install/ENTRYPOINT reference
install-autodeploy.sh matches none of the conventions globs (materialize-*.sh / *-entrypoint.sh / compose-up.sh)
Because it is never in `derived`, `uncovered()`'s `path not in exclusions` guard is never reached for it
advisory.finding: The single EXCLUSIONS entry, `infra/scripts/install-autodeploy.sh`, is never produced by any of the three derivation sources (it is not COPY/install/ENTRYPOINT-referenced in any Dockerfile.*/compose, and does not match materialize-*.sh / *-entrypoint.sh / compose-up.sh), so the exclusion suppresses nothing and the mechanism's stated premise ('derived but intentionally NOT deploy-triggering') does not hold for it. It is effectively inert documentation that the file-existence check happens to keep green.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Exclude the COPY destination (last token) from the `.sh` source-token extraction so a `.sh`-named destination is not mis-derived.
evidence: scripts/check_deploy_manifest.py:145-146: `source, label = stripped.split(None, 1)[1], 'COPY'` then `tokens = [t for t in source.split() if t.endswith('.sh')]` — includes the final (destination) argument
current COPYs (`COPY . /app`, `COPY --from=... /uv ...`) contain no `.sh` token so the bug is not exercised today
advisory.finding: In `_derive_from_dockerfile`, the `COPY` branch filters every whitespace-split token ending in `.sh`, which includes the COPY DESTINATION, not just sources. A directive like `COPY foo.sh /opt/bar.sh` would attempt to resolve the destination `/opt/bar.sh` as a repo path. No current Dockerfile triggers this, so it is latent, but the ENTRYPOINT/install branches use `_iter_sh_tokens` which has the same source/dest-agnostic behavior.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a synthetic test that drives `_derive_from_compose` with a docker-compose fragment containing `entrypoint:`/`command:` referencing a repo .sh script and assert the path+source are derived.
evidence: search of tests/unit/test_check_deploy_manifest.py for `_derive_from` and `_iter_sh_tokens` returned `(no matches)`

search of infra/compose/docker-compose.yml for `command:` returned `(no matches)`; the only CMD-like lines are `test: ["CMD", ...]` healthchecks (docker-compose.yml:291,529) which do not match `^(entrypoint|command):`

Named violating input: a compose service `command: ["./infra/scripts/materialize-foo.sh"]` referencing a deploy-relevant script would exercise lines 160-172, but no test drives that path so a matcher regression there is undetected.
scripts/check_deploy_manifest.py:135: `def _iter_sh_tokens(value: str)` — strips `"[](),'\""` and filters `".sh" in tok`
search of tests/unit/test_check_deploy_manifest.py for `_iter_sh_tokens` returned `(no matches)`

Real Dockerfiles use `CMD ["rebar-mcp"]` / `CMD ["uvicorn", ...]` (Dockerfile.mcp:151, Dockerfile.opcert:47) — no `.sh` token, so the `.sh`-extraction path in _iter_sh_tokens is not meaningfully exercised for CMD/ENTRYPOINT array forms.
advisory.finding: The compose-directive derivation branch `_derive_from_compose` (added lines 160-172) is never exercised by any test. The real `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml` contains no `entrypoint:`/`command:` service directives (only `test: ["CMD", ...]` healthcheck lines, which do NOT match the `^(entrypoint|command):` regex), so the real-repo derivation never enters this function's match body; and no synthetic test drives compose parsing. A deploy-relevant script referenced only via a compose `command: ["./infra/scripts/materialize-foo.sh"]` (or a regression breaking that matcher) would silently fail to derive — the exact fail-open class this gate exists to prevent.
merged_from: The `_iter_sh_tokens` helper and the Dockerfile `ENTRYPOINT`/`CMD` JSON-array `.sh`-token extraction branch are not unit-tested in isolation. The ENTRYPOINT branch is only incidentally covered via Dockerfile.mcp's real ENTRYPOINT; token-extraction edge cases (JSON-array quoting/bracket stripping, multi-token CMD, the `install -m` shell form) have no direct assertion.
scenarios: A future compose service adds an entrypoint/command referencing a deploy-relevant .sh script
A refactor of `_derive_from_compose`'s regex or token extraction silently stops matching
